reasoning: For a proposed separation, each rooted subtree keeps a maximum-cardinality packing and maximizes its nearest selected distance among ties. Merge child packings in increasing nearest distance: when the closest two conflict, discard the closer selected vertex. Any other selected vertex from that same child is farther than the retained closest vertex by the within-child separation invariant, so no extra child state is needed. Once the nearest remaining vertex is far enough, add the current root. The resulting maximum count is monotone in the proposed distance, enabling integer binary search.
